sentences.text: Respondents Date of institution of appeal : 03.07.2014 Date on which reserved for judgment : 16.10.2014 Date on which judgment was passed : 31.10.2014 JUDGMENT 1.

The present appeal is directed against the impugned order dated 07.06.2014 passed by the court of Ld Senior Civil Judge/RC, South West, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi, in the suit No. 75/14 titled as "Sharda Jain Vs. Manager BSES RPL & another whereby an application under Order 39 Rule 1 & 2 of the respondent no. 1/plaintiff was allowed, thereby directing the officials of the respondent no. 2,
who were defendant No. 1, in the trial court, to provide an electricity connection to the respondent no. 1/plaintiff at the suit property without insisting upon the documents of the property and NOC from the appellant/defendant no. 2. Aggrieved with the impugned order dated 7.06.2014 of ld SCJ/RC, South West, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi, the appellant preferred the present appeal.

It is further averred by the respondent no. 1/plaintiff in her plaint that she has bought the said premises from one builder namely Sh. Ram Singh Aggarwal ie the appellant/defendant no.
2, who had already given the possession of the said premises on 12.06.2013 but failed to execute the sale deed in favour of the respondent no. 1/plaintiff, despite of taking substantial amount for the sale of the said premises, and for which respondent no. 1/plaintiff has also filed suit for permanent and mandatory injunction as well against the builder ie. appellant/defendant no. 2, before the court of Ld. ASCJ, Dwarka Courts.
3. As per respondent no. 1/plaintiff, the respondent no. 2, who was defendant no. 1 in the Ld. trial court, is the supplier of the electricity for domestic consumption in the locality.
Respondent no.

1/Plaintiff stated to have applied for electricity connection for the purpose of the domestic consumption online on 18.02.2014 and she was also provided the reference number 8001301332,
however, respondent no. 2/defendant(BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd.) failed to give connection to the respondent no. 1/plaintiff on the pretext that respondent no. 1/plaintiff is not the valid/registered owner of the premises and they showed their inability to provide the power connection to the respondent no. 1/ plaintiff for want of the said requirement.

It is also alleged by the respondent no.
1/plaintiff that the builder Sh. Ram Singh Aggarwal ie. appellant/defendant no. 2 failed to provide the NOC to the respondent no. 1/plaintiff for the purpose of seeking electricity connection.

4. The respondent no. 2/ BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd in its WS taken the objection that the respondent no. 1/plaintiff has no title documents in respect to the suit premises and hence, as per the DERC Rule for fresh electricity connection the plaintiff is required the NOC from the appellant/defendant no. 2.
5.

The respondent no.1/plaintiff also filed an application under Order 39 Rule 1 and 2 read with section 151 CPC, before the trial court, thereby praying for directions to the officials of respondent no. 2/defendant(BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd.) to install electricity connection at the premises of the respondent no. 1/plaintiff in the suit premises ie. at WZ-1203A, First Floor, front side, palam village,
New Delhi-45.

Thereafter, the ld trial court vide order dated 07.06.2014 allowed the application of the respondent no. 1/plaintiff and directed the respondent no. 2 who were defendant no 1 in the trial court, to provide an electricity connection to respondent no. 1/plaintiff in the aforesaid suit premises, without insisting upon a sale deed or documents in the nature of GPA etc. and without requiring NOC from appellant/defendant no. 2.
6.

Aggrieved by the impugned order passed by ld. Senior Civil Judge, the appellant has filed the present appeal challenging the impugned order on the ground that ld. Trial court has no jurisdiction to entertain and adjudicate upon the alleged claim of the respondent no.1/plaintiff.
The impugned order has also been assailed by the appellant contending that the civil court jurisdiction has been barred under the DERC Regulations.

The appellant also challenged the impugned order contending that the ld. Trial court has exercised outside its jurisdiction by decreeing the suit in the form of grant of relief of temporary injunction by invoking provisions enumerated in order XXXIX Rule 1 and 2 of CPC, whereas, the ld. Trial court has not empowered under law to grant final relief by invoking the aforesaid order.

Among other grounds, the impugned order is also assailed contending that the disputed question of facts cannot be adjudicated in summarily specially when the onus to prove its Ram Singh Aggarwal vs Smt Sharda Jain on 31 October, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15367821/
2 case is upon the plaintiff.

sentences.text: 7. I have heard the arguments of ld. Counsel for the appellant as well as ld. Counsels for respondents.
8. Ld. Counsel for appellants submitted that the ld trial court has no jurisdiction to try, entertain and adjudicate upon the alleged claim of respondent no. 1/plaintiff.

It is also argued by ld counsel for appellant that the respondent no.1 claims that her application was declined to be processed by BSES, however, the BSES is governed by the regulations of DERC(Performance Standards Metering & Billing) Regulations, 2004, and as such, if she has any grievances against the said denial, then, she can lodge her grievances before the officials appointed under the aforesaid DERC Regulations.

He also argued that the impugned order passed by the ld trial court giving directions to the BSES to provide electricity connection to the respondent no 1/plaintiff, that also, without filing necessary documents, is per se illegal as the directions issued by the ld trial court are not in its domain as jurisdiction of civil court is barred.

Ld counsel for appellant also argued that the ld trial court has exercised outside its jurisdiction by decreeing the suit in the form of grant of relief of temporary injunction by invoking under Order XXXIX Rule 1 and 2 CPC, whereas, the ld. Trial court is not empowered under law to grant final relief by invoking the aforesaid provisions.

Counsel for appellant also argued that at no point of time, the possession of the suit property was handed over by the appellant to respondent no. 1/plaintiff and as such the respondent no. 1/plaintiff is a trespasser and also alleged bayana receipts as relied upon by the respondent no. 1/plaintiff are forged and fabricated documents.
Counsel for appellant submitted that the impugned order is liable to be set aside and prayed that appeal may be allowed.

9. On the other hand, ld. Counsel for respondent no.1/plaintiff submitted that respondent no.
1/plaintiff has bought the suit property from the appellant, who had given the possession of the suit property to her on 12.06.2013 and thereafter, the appellant failed to execute the sale deed in favour of respondent no. 1.
It is also contended by the counsel for the respondent no. 1/plaintiff that the respondent no 1/plaintiff is in settled possession of the suit property since 12.06.2013.

He also submitted that the respondent no. 2/BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd has illegally and unlawfully denied the power connection to the respondent no. 1 /plaintiff on the flimsy ground with ulterior motives that the respondent no. 1/plaintiff is not having title of the premises.
He further submitted that there is no infirmity in the order of ld. trial court as the ld. trial court has passed very reasoned order.
Counsel for the respondent no. 1 submitted that instant appeal is liable to be dismissed.

10. Counsel for respondent no. 2 submitted that the application for respondent no. 1/plaintiff for electricity connection had been rejected on the ground that respondent no.1/plaintiff had not furnished the ownership documents of the suit property.

It is further submitted by counsel for respondent no. 2 that the respondent no. 1/plaintiff has also not furnished the commercial formalities for new connection as per the DERC Rules and further, as per DERC Rules, the respondent no. 1/plaintiff was also required the NOC from appellant/defendant no.2.
11.
I have considered the rival submissions of the Ld. Counsel for the parties and also gone through the record and perused the file.

sentences.text:
The ld trial court vide order dated 07.06.2014 allowed the application of the respondent no.
1/plaintiff under Order XXXIX Rule 1 and 2 CPC, thereby directing the respondent no. 2(Manager BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd) to provide electricity connection to the respondent no. 1/plaintiff in the suit property, without insisting upon a sale deed or GPA and without requiring NOC from appellant/defendant no. 2.

While allowing the aforesaid application of the respondent no.
1/plaintiff
, the Ld. trial court also directed the respondent no. 1/plaintiff to comply with necessary commercial formalities.
However, it is the contention of the appellant that while passing the impugned order, the ld trial court has exercised outside its jurisdiction.
It is also the contention of the appellant that respondent no. 1/plaintiff has yet to establish its ownership and possession over the suit property.

It is also the contention of the appellant that the civil court has no jurisdiction to entertain the suit filed by respondent no.1/plaintiff as the DERC Regulations prohibits the jurisdiction of the civil court, particularly, for the relief as sought by the respondent no. 1/plaintiff in its suit.
13. The respondent no. 1/plaintiff has also filed the copies of bayana receipts dated 08.01.2012 along with the suit before the trial court.

As per the aforesaid bayana receipts dated 08.1.2012, the appellant and respondent no 1/plaintiff entered into an agreement for the sale of suit property for total consideration of Rs. 50 lacs in respect of the sale of first floor, front side flat, in khasra no.
33/2/3 measuring 130 sq. yards.
Though, in the suit the respondent no. 1/plaintiff has given the number of the suit property as WZ-1203-A, First floor, front side, Palam Village-45.
However, in the said bayana receipt the name of the appellant and the respondent no. 1/plaintiff has been mentioned as seller and purchaser of the property respectively.

Moreover, the description of the property ie.
First Floor, front side at Palam Village also creates strong resemblance between the description of suit property as mentioned in the plaint and in the bayana receipt dated 08.01.2012.
It is the contention of the respondent no. 1/plaintiff that she is residing in the suit premises since 12.06.2013 when the possession was delivered to her by the appellant.
The respondent no. 1/plaintiff has also filed documents relating to gas connection in her name which shows the address of the respondent no. 1/plaintiff as WZ-1203A, F/F, Palam Village, New Delhi-45.

This document of gas connection of Hindustan Petroleum Co-op. Ltd is a vital document in respect of the claim of the respondent no.
1/plaintiff that she is residing in the suit premises since 12.06.2013 as in the said document, the address of the respondent no. 1/plaintiff is same as mentioned in the suit.

Further, I have also perused the copy of pass book of the husband of the respondent no. 1/plaintiff as well as intimation regarding pan card of husband of respondent no. 1/plaintiff which also shows the same address as reflected in the suit.
Hence, there is force in the contention of the respondent no. 1/plaintiff that she is residing in the suit premises.
14. The electricity is an essential item without which a person cannot live normal life and without electricity, a person is bound to face many hardships in life.

In the judgment of Smt. S.Padma Vs.
Central Electricity Supply Utility (CESU), Odisha decided by Hon'ble High Court of Odisha on 30.11.2012, in WP(C) 11358/12 observed as under:-

Smt. S.Padma Vs.
Central Electricity Supply Utility (CESU), Odisha

sentences.text: "15. Needless to say that right to shelter is a fundamental right under Article 19(1) of the Constitution of India(See Chameli Singh others Vs. State of U.P and another AIR 1996 SC 1051) and shelter without electricity makes the life miserable.

Electricity is the basic necessity for survival of a Ram Singh Aggarwal vs Smt Sharda Jain on 31 October, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15367821/
4 person in modern days.

sentences.text: Abrupt disconnection of power supply or non-supply of power seriously affects a person's right to have his food, water and decent environment, medical care and education.
Disconnection of power supply from the premises of a consumer or non-supply of power to an applicant has a drastic impact on the day-to-day life of the citizens.

It affects study of children,
enhances the misery of old and sick persons, endangers the safety of the houses more particularly it is unbearable in the present days of global warming."
15.

Further, in the judgment titled as Sh. Chandu Khamaru Vs Nayan Malik & ors, decided by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal no. 7572/2011 arising out of SLP(C) No. 15332 of 2008,
dated 02.09.2011, while discussing the various provisions of Electricity Act, 2003, observed as under:-

entities.text: Sh. Chandu Khamaru Vs Nayan Malik & ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "Sub section (1) of section 43 provides that every distribution licensee, shall, on an application by the owner or occupier of any premises, give supply of electricity to such premises, within one month after receipt of the application requiring such supply.

These provisions in the Electricity Act, 2003 make it amply clear that a distribution licensee has a statutory duty to supply electricity to an owner or occupier of any premises located in the area of supply of electricity of the distribution licensee,
if such owner or occupier of the premises applies for it, and correspondingly every owner or occupier of any premises has a statutory right to apply for and obtain such electric supply from the distribution licensee."

16. Therefore, from the abovesaid case law, it is amply clear that it is the duty of the distribution licensee to supply and provide the electricity to an owner or occupier of any premises located in the area of supply of electricity of the distribution licensee, if such owner or occupier of the premises applies for the same.

In the instant matter, the respondent no. 1/plaintiff applied for electricity connection before the Manager, BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd, i .e. respondent no. 2 who was defendant no. 1 in the trial court.

However, the respondent no. 2/Manager, BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd failed to provide electricity connection to the respondent no. 1/plaintiff on the ground that the respondent no. 1/plaintiff has no title document in respect of the suit premises and hence, as per the DRC Rules,
for fresh electricity connection, the respondent no. 1/plaintiff is required the NOC from the appellant/defendant no. 2.
17.
The respondent no. 1/plaintiff has prima facie able to show that she is in possession of the suit premises and residing there in the said premises.

As such, the respondent no. 2/BSES Rajdhani Power ltd., cannot deny the electricity connection to the respondent no. 1/plaintiff on the aforesaid ground of documents of the suit premises and NOC from the appellant, as it is the statutory duty of the respondent no. 2/BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd, to provide electricity connection to the respondent no. 1/plaintiff.
As discussed above, electricity is the basic necessity for a person, without which the life can become miserable and a person cannot lead a normal life.
Moreover, respondent no. 2/BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd cannot absolve from its responsibility to provide electricity to the respondent no. 1/plaintiff.
Hence, it is the duty of the respondent no. 2/BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd to provide electricity connection to the respondent no. 1/plaintiff.
